title: p256-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho on negation classes with a sigma walk

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and input Q=[x]P on NIST P-256, the parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39. It walks on the negation classes {W,-W}, using 2^32 walks, 2^16 adders, batched affine additions (Montgomery simultaneous inversion, 5M+1S per step) and deterministic fruitless-cycle escapes. Walks run in trails from fresh coins: each trail ends at its first distinguished point, which it records once with its coins, and the first key match is resolved by replaying the two trails, so a degenerate match has probability exactly 1/r (Lemmas R and D) and the replay is bounded and charged. The walk stores actual points and adds +-R_i from a table according to the parity of the Montgomery y, so the class sequence equals the standard canonical walk while no point is negated. Total computation is at most 2^127.273624 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, distinguished-point storage and lookup, all failures and restarts, collision replay, verification and output. No reference operation is used: every instruction, including all P-256 field arithmetic, is charged at 1/C with the borrowed C=1000. Each walk step is charged 830 scalar AArch64 instructions against 819.9 and 820.6 measured with the organizer's Callgrind toolchain; field multiplication is Montgomery arithmetic in inline AArch64 assembly (p = -1 mod 2^64, so reduction uses shifts and adds). Peak memory is at most 2^76.542441 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^48.619436 units and is included in total work. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack on one target with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. The success bound of 0.411523 relies on the disclosed heuristics H1-H3 in proof.md: H1 the standard random-mapping model for r-adding class walks with an exponent penalty of at most 4/2^16, H2 bounds on fruitless-cycle rates, H3 the representativeness of the measured instruction counts. These are supported by toy-curve runs of the identical procedure and by production-curve measurements, not proved. This is a carefully accounted generic attack, not a claim of a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the complete procedure of proof.md section 1.3 on random prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3-3x+b (the P-256 shape), at budget tau = tau_e4/10^4: each slot runs trails from fresh coins without tracking coefficients, with the same class key, canonical rule, adder images and index, both cycle rules and escapes; a trail ends at its first distinguished point, recorded once with its coins, or is abandoned at the cap; each slot takes L steps and finishes its trail. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails from their coins (with a different anchor schedule, checking Lemma R); a degenerate match fails. Reports the success rate against 1-exp(-tau), degenerate matches and replay mismatches. No oracle collision table. Toy scale only: it tests the procedure and its collision statistics, not production cost.
Recompute the claimed time_log2, preprocessing, memory and success lower bound from the stated parameters with exact integer arithmetic.
